ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in Figure 1, the parabola $y=-x^2+bx+c$ intersects the x-axis at points A and B, and intersects the y-axis at point C (0, 3). The axis of symmetry is the line $x=1$, which intersects the x-axis at point D, and the vertex is point E. As shown in Figure 2, point F is on the y-axis, and $OF=\sqrt{2}$, point N is a moving point on the parabola within the first quadrant, and is to the right of the parabola's axis of symmetry. The line ON intersects the axis of symmetry at point G, and line GF is drawn. If GF bisects $\angle OGE$, find the coordinates of point N.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let $FP \perp DE$ at point P through point F, thus $FP=1$. Draw $FQ \perp ON$ at Q through point F, \\
since $GF$ bisects $\angle OGE$, \\
therefore $FQ=FP=1$, \\
in $\triangle FQO$, $OF= \sqrt{2}$, \\
according to the Pythagorean theorem, we get $OQ=\sqrt{OF^{2}-FQ^{2}}=1$, \\
thus $OQ=FQ$, \\
thus $\angle FOQ=45^\circ$, \\
thus $\angle BON=90^\circ-45^\circ=45^\circ$, \\
draw $QM \perp OB$ at M through point Q, $OM=QM$ \\
therefore, the equation of $ON$ is $y=x$, \\
since point N lies on the parabola $y=-x^{2}+2x+3$, \\
by solving the system $\begin{cases}y=x\\ y=-x^{2}+2x+3\end{cases}$, \\
we obtain $\left\{\begin{array}{l}x=\frac{1+\sqrt{13}}{2}\\ y=\frac{1+\sqrt{13}}{2}\end{array}\right\}$ or $\left\{\begin{array}{l}x=\frac{1-\sqrt{13}}{2}\\ y=\frac{1-\sqrt{13}}{2}\end{array}\right\}$ (since point N is to the right of the axis of symmetry $x=1$, the latter is discarded), \\
thus, the coordinates of point N are: $\left(\boxed{\frac{1+\sqrt{13}}{2}}, \boxed{\frac{1+\sqrt{13}}{2}}\right)$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure contains Figure 1 and Figure 2, both drawing a parabola opening downward and coordinate axes. In Figure 1, the parabola intersects the x-axis at A and B, intersects the y-axis at C, and passes through the vertical axis of symmetry x=1; this axis of symmetry intersects the x-axis at D, and the vertex is E. In Figure 2, F is located on the positive y-axis, N is located on the right branch of the parabola and in the first quadrant, the line ON starts from the origin O and passes through N, and intersects the vertical axis of symmetry x=1 at G, and line segment GF connects F and G. The problem states that GF bisects ∠OGE. Reasoning: The parabola is y=-x^2+bx+c. Because the parabola intersects the y-axis at C(0,3), substituting x=0 gives c=3. The axis of symmetry of the parabola y=-x^2+bx+c is x=b/2. The problem states that the axis of symmetry is x=1, so b/2=1, b=2. Therefore the equation of the parabola is y=-x^2+2x+3. Because GE is on the vertical line x=1, and F is on the y-axis, that is, x=0, the perpendicular distance from point F to GE is 1. Also because GF bisects ∠OGE, and F is on the angle bisector, the perpendicular distance from F to the other side GO of the angle is also 1; and GO and ON are the same straight line. Draw FQ⊥ON through F, with foot of the perpendicular Q, then FQ=1. In right triangle OFQ, OF=√2, FQ=1, so OQ=√(OF^2-FQ^2)=√(2-1)=1. Thus OQ=FQ, triangle OFQ is an isosceles right triangle, and ∠FOQ=45°. Since OF is along the y-axis direction and ON is in the first quadrant, ON also forms a 45° angle with the positive direction of the x-axis; therefore the equation of line ON is y=x. Point N is simultaneously on line ON and on the parabola, so combining y=x and y=-x^2+2x+3 gives x=-x^2+2x+3, namely x^2-x-3=0. Solving gives x=(1±√13)/2, and y=x. Because N is on the right side of the axis of symmetry x=1, take the root x>1, x=(1+√13)/2. Therefore the coordinates of N are ((1+√13)/2,(1+√13)/2).
